127776.e: The property color sets the font colour, for example color: red. The other properties control alignment, spacing and borders.
127776.m: In CSS you set the text colour with color.

127777.q: Which CSS property sets the background colour?
127777.e: With background-color you colour the background of an element. There is no property called text-color in CSS.
127777.m: You colour the background with background-color.

127778.q: What do you use a class such as .important for in CSS?
a: To give many elements the same design
To make the page load faster
127778.e: A class selector such as .important targets all elements with class="important". This way you design many elements with a single rule.
127778.m: In CSS you write classes with a full stop in front.

127779.q: How often should an ID such as id="title" appear on a web page?
127779.e: An ID is like a name that belongs to only one element. In CSS you target it with a hash sign, for example #title.
127779.m: In CSS you select an ID with the hash sign.

127780.q: Which CSS property changes the font size?
127780.e: With font-size you set how big a text appears, for example font-size: 20px. The other names are not valid CSS properties.
127780.m: You set the font size with font-size.

127781.q: What is the difference between margin and padding in CSS?
a: margin is the outer spacing, padding the inner spacing
margin is the colour, padding the font
margin is the border, padding the shadow
margin only applies to pictures, padding only to text
127781.e: In the box model, padding lies between the content and the border, margin outside the border. This lets you control spacing exactly.
127781.m: Padding is inside, margin is outside.

127782.q: Where do you usually include an external CSS file in the HTML page?
a: In the head section with the link element
Right at the end in the footer element
127782.e: With <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> in the head section a CSS file is loaded. This way the design applies to the whole page.
127782.m: You link a CSS file in the head section with the link element.

127783.q: Which HTML element makes the largest heading?
127783.e: Headings go from <h1> to <h6>, with <h1> being the most important and largest. <h6> is the smallest level.
127783.m: The most important heading on a page goes in h1.

127784.q: Which HTML element stands for a paragraph of text?
127784.e:
The p stands for paragraph. The text goes between

and

.
127784.m: In HTML a paragraph is marked up with p.

127785.q: Which HTML element do you use to include a picture?
127785.e: The element shows a picture; you give the picture file in the src attribute. It needs no closing tag.
127785.m: In HTML you include pictures with img.

127786.q: Which attribute of describes the picture in words for people who cannot see it?
127786.e: The alternative text in the alt attribute is read aloud by screen readers, for example. It also appears if the picture cannot be loaded.
127786.m: Every picture needs a descriptive alt text.

127787.q: Which HTML element creates an unordered list with bullet points?
127787.e: ul stands for unordered list. The individual entries each go in <li> elements.
127787.m: A list with bullet points begins with ul.

127788.q: Which HTML element do you use for a numbered list?
127788.e: ol stands for ordered list. The browser numbers the entries automatically.
127788.m: You write a numbered list with ol.

127789.e: stands for break and starts a new line without starting a new paragraph. It has no closing tag.
127789.m: With br you force a line break.

127790.q:
How do you write the closing tag for

?
127790.e: A closing tag has a slash after the angle bracket. Together with the opening tag it surrounds the content.
127790.m: A closing tag starts with a slash after the bracket.

127791.q: Which HTML element sets the text shown in the browser tab?
127791.e: The <title> element goes in the head section. Its content appears in the tab and also in search engine results.
127791.m: The text in the browser tab comes from the title element.

127792.q: Which HTML element do you use to create a link?
127792.e: The a stands for anchor. The text between and becomes clickable.
127792.m: In HTML you write links with the a element.

127793.q: Which attribute contains the destination of a link?
127793.e: The href attribute contains the address the link leads to. href comes from hypertext reference.
127793.m: The destination of a link goes in the href attribute.

127794.q: What does target="_blank" do on a link?
a: The page opens in a new tab
127794.e: With target="_blank" the browser opens the destination in a new tab or window. The original page stays open.
127794.m: With target="_blank" a link opens a new tab.

a: A link that points from the location of the current page
A link with a complete web address
A link that only works on Sundays
A link to a telephone number
127795.e: A relative link such as pictures/photo.html gives the path starting from the current file. An absolute link contains the complete address with the domain.
127795.m: Relative links describe the path from the current page.

127796.q: What is a link called that no longer works because the destination is missing?
127796.e: A dead link leads nowhere; often the error message 404 then appears. Websites should be checked regularly for dead links.
127796.m: A dead link points to a page that no longer exists.

127797.q: Which link destination makes a click open the email program?
127797.e: A link such as <a href="mailto:info@example.ch"> opens a new email window with the address. This lets people get in touch.
127797.m: A link with mailto opens the email program.

127798.q: How do you link to a particular place with id="contact" on the same page?
127798.e: A hash sign with the ID name jumps to the matching place on the page. This is called a jump link or anchor.
127798.m: With a hash sign a link jumps to a place on the page.

127799.q: What is text called that is connected to other texts by links?
127799.e: Hypertext is text with references to other texts. You jump from one text to the next with a click.
127799.m: Texts connected by links are called hypertext.

127800.q: What is the main job of a web browser?
127800.e: A browser loads HTML, CSS, pictures and scripts from servers and uses them to display the web page. Well-known browsers include Firefox, Chrome and Safari.
127800.m: A web browser fetches web pages and shows them.

127801.q: What does the address bar of a web browser show?
a: The address of the page that is open
127801.e: The address bar shows the URL of the current page, for example https://www.example.ch. You can also type in an address there yourself.
127801.m: The address bar shows the URL of the current page.

127802.q: What is Apple's web browser called?
127802.e: Safari comes pre-installed on iPhones, iPads and Macs. Edge comes from Microsoft and Chrome from Google.
127802.m: Apple's web browser is called Safari.

127803.q: What does a browser do with the HTML code of a web page?
a: It turns it into a visible page
It deletes it without reading it
It sends it to all your contacts
127803.e: The browser reads the code and works out how texts, pictures and buttons should look. Then it shows the finished page.
127803.m: The browser turns code into a visible page.

127804.q: What does a browser store in its cache?
a: Copies of loaded files for faster access
127804.e: The browser keeps pictures, scripts and other files in the cache. If you visit the page again, it does not need to download them again.
127804.m: The cache makes familiar pages load faster.

127805.q: What is a cookie in connection with web browsers?
a: A small file with data from a website
127805.e: Websites use cookies to store small pieces of information in the browser, such as whether you are logged in. Some cookies are also used to track users across several sites.
127805.m: Cookies are small packets of data that websites put in the browser.

127806.q: What are the developer tools in a browser for?
a: To examine the code of a page and find errors
127806.e: With the developer tools you can look at and test a page's HTML, CSS and JavaScript. In many browsers you open them with the F12 key.
127806.m: Developer tools help you examine web pages.

127807.q: What does a browser's private or incognito mode do?
a: History and cookies are deleted after closing
You are completely invisible on the internet
127807.e: In private mode the browser does not keep history and cookies after closing. Websites, your school or your internet provider can still see what you do.
127807.m: Private mode only protects on your own device, not on the whole internet.

127808.q: Which country ending does Switzerland have in internet addresses?
127808.e: .ch comes from Confoederatio Helvetica, the Latin name for Switzerland. .cz is the ending for Czechia.

127809.q: What is the last part of a domain, such as .ch or .com, called?
127809.e: The top-level domain is at the far right of a domain. There are country endings like .ch and general ones like .com or .org.
127809.m: The ending of a domain is called the top-level domain.

127810.q: Which system translates domain names into IP addresses?
127810.e: DNS works like the internet's telephone directory. For a name like example.ch it finds the matching IP address of the server.
127810.m: The DNS is the telephone directory of the internet.

127811.q: Which ending belongs to the Principality of Liechtenstein?
127811.e: .li is the country ending for Liechtenstein. .lt belongs to Lithuania and .lu to Luxembourg.

127812.q: In the address school.example.ch, what is the part “school”?
127812.e: A subdomain goes to the left of the actual domain. It lets you separate areas of a website, such as shop.example.ch.
127812.m: Whatever is to the left of the domain is a subdomain.

127813.q: What do you have to do to get your own domain?
a: Have it registered with a provider
Simply type it into the browser
Apply for it from the Federal Council
Enter it in the telephone directory
127813.e: Domains are registered through registrars and usually paid for every year. In Switzerland a .ch domain usually costs only a few francs a year.
127813.m: You have to register and pay for your own domain.

127814.q: Which ending was originally meant for commercial websites?
127814.e: .com stands for commercial. .edu is used for universities in the USA and .gov for US authorities.

127815.q: What happens if two people want to register the same domain?
a: Only one person can get it
Both get it at the same time
The domain automatically gets a number
127815.e: Every domain is unique worldwide. Usually whoever registers it first gets it.

127816.q: What does a web server do?
a: It delivers web pages to browsers
It shows web pages on the screen
It writes new web pages automatically
127816.e: A web server waits for requests from browsers and sends back the files they want. The browser then shows them.
127816.m: A web server answers requests from browsers.

127817.q: What does the abbreviation HTTP stand for?
127817.e: HTTP is the protocol that browsers and web servers use to exchange data. It sets out what requests and responses look like.
127817.m: HTTP is the language between browser and web server.

127819.q: Which error code shows that a page was not found?
127819.e: The status code 404 means Not Found. The code 500, on the other hand, means an error on the server.
127819.m: The error 404 means the page was not found.

127820.q: Why is a web server usually switched on day and night?
a: So that the website can be reached at any time
So that it does not break
So that it uses less electricity
So that it writes web pages itself
127820.e: Browsers all over the world can request a page at any time of day. If the server is switched off, it cannot answer.
127820.m: A web server runs all the time so that websites can always be reached.

127821.q: What is the principle called in which a browser requests something and a server answers?
127821.e: The browser is the client that requests something. The server provides the data and answers.
127821.m: On the web the client asks and the server answers.

127822.q: Which software is a well-known web server?
127822.e: The Apache HTTP Server is widely used, free web server software. Thunderbird is an email program, Audacity an audio program.
127822.m: Apache is well-known web server software.

127823.q: What does a web hosting provider offer?
a: Storage space and servers for websites
127823.e: A web host provides storage on servers that are permanently connected to the internet. This means you do not have to run your own server.
127823.m: With web hosting you rent space on a server for your website.

a: A website is printed on paper
You share your password with friends
A website only runs on your own phone
127824.e: With shared hosting, many websites are on the same server. This is cheap, but the performance is shared.
127824.m: With shared hosting many websites share one server.

127825.q: What is it called when you rent a whole server just for yourself?
127825.e: A dedicated server is available to only one customer. It offers more performance and control, but costs more.
127825.m: A whole server just for yourself is called a dedicated server.

127826.q: Which protocol is traditionally used to upload files to web space?
127826.e: FTP means File Transfer Protocol and is used to transfer files. Today people often use the encrypted version, SFTP.
127826.m: Files are often uploaded to the server by FTP or SFTP.

127827.q: Where are web hosts' servers usually located?
127827.e: Data centres provide cooling, emergency power and fast internet connections. This keeps the websites reliably reachable.
127827.m: Web servers are usually in well-secured data centres.

127828.q: In web hosting, what does the storage space figure mean?
a: How much data you may store on the server
How many visitors arrive per second
127828.e: Storage space limits how big all the files of the website may be together. Pictures and videos need especially a lot of space.
127828.m: Storage space tells you how much data fits on the web space.

127829.q: Why is the location of the data centre important for some Swiss companies?
a: Because of data protection under Swiss law
Because websites would otherwise be displayed wrongly
Because otherwise the .ch domain is forbidden
Because the colours would otherwise look different
127829.e: If a server is in Switzerland, Swiss law applies to the data. That is why some companies deliberately choose hosting in Switzerland.
127829.m: The server location affects which data protection law applies.

127830.q: What is a backup in web hosting?
a: A safety copy of the website data
127830.e: A backup is a safety copy. If something breaks or gets deleted, you can use it to restore the website.
127830.m: Regular backups protect a website from losing data.

127831.q: What does responsive web design mean?
a: The page adapts to the screen size
The page is only black and white
127831.e: With responsive web design, the content rearranges itself depending on the device. That way a page is easy to read on a phone, tablet and computer.
127831.m: Responsive pages look good on every screen.

127832.q: Which CSS technique do you use to react to different screen widths?
127832.e: With a media query such as @media (max-width: 600px), certain rules only apply on narrow screens. That way you can adapt the layout.
127832.m: Media queries adapt the layout to the screen width.

127833.q: What does the Mobile First approach mean?
a: You design for small screens first
You only test on the computer
127833.e: With Mobile First, you plan the view for smartphones first. Then you extend the layout for bigger screens.
127833.m: Mobile First means starting with the smallest screen.

127834.q: What often happens when a web page is not responsive and you open it on a phone?
a: It becomes tiny or sticks out over the edge
It cannot be opened at all
127834.e: A page built only for big screens does not fit on a narrow phone. You then have to zoom or swipe sideways.
127834.m: Without responsive design, pages are hard to read on phones.

127835.q: Which width setting for a picture adapts to the width of the screen?
a: Half the width of the window
127835.e: A setting relative to the window width grows and shrinks with the screen. Fixed sizes such as 800 pixels are often too wide on a phone.
127835.m: Relative widths adapt to the screen.

127836.q: Why are widths in responsive layouts often given in per cent?
a: So that elements adapt to the available width
So that the page loads faster
So that the colours become stronger
So that the text becomes bold
127836.e: A width of 50% is always half as wide as the surrounding element. Fixed pixel widths, on the other hand, often do not fit on small screens.

127837.q: Which CSS layout system arranges elements in rows and columns like a grid?
127837.e: With display: grid you create a grid of rows and columns. It is well suited to responsive layouts.
127837.m: CSS Grid arranges content in a grid.

127838.q: Which CSS layout model arranges elements flexibly in a row or column?
127838.e: With display: flex you spread elements out in a row or column. With flex-wrap they can move to the next line when there is little space.
127838.m: Flexbox arranges elements flexibly in one direction.

127839.q: What do you call the screen width at which a responsive layout changes?
127839.e: At a breakpoint, for example at 768 pixels, the layout switches, say, from one column to two columns. The page then looks different on a phone than on a computer.
127839.m: At a breakpoint the layout changes.

127840.q: What is the aim of an accessible internet?
a: Everyone should be able to use websites
127840.e: Accessible websites can also be used by people with visual, hearing or other impairments. Often everyone else benefits too.

a: A program that reads out what is on the screen
127841.e: Blind and visually impaired people have content read out by a screen reader or shown on a Braille display. For this, the page needs a clean structure.
127841.m: Screen readers read web pages aloud for blind people.

127842.q: What are the international WCAG guidelines for?
a: To make websites accessible to everyone
To make websites show more adverts
127842.e: WCAG stands for Web Content Accessibility Guidelines and comes from the W3C. The rules help to make websites accessible. Switzerland follows them too.
127842.m: The WCAG are the most important rules for accessible websites.

127843.q: Why is enough colour contrast between text and background important?
a: So that people with poor eyesight can read the text too
So that the page loads faster
So that the page uses less electricity
So that the domain becomes cheaper
127843.e: Light grey text on a white background is hard for many people to read. Strong contrast especially helps people with a visual impairment.
127843.m: Good contrast makes text readable for everyone.

127844.q: Why should a website also work without a mouse?
a: Because some people can only use the keyboard
Because web servers do not know about mice
127844.e: People with physical disabilities or blind people often use the computer with the keyboard only. With the Tab key they jump from element to element.
127844.m: A good website can be used with the keyboard alone.

127845.q: Why should you not show information only through colour, for example red boxes for errors?
a: Because some people cannot tell colours apart
Because red does not work on all screens
Because colours slow the page down
127845.e: People with colour blindness, for example, find it hard to tell red and green apart. That is why you add text or symbols to colours.
127845.m: Important messages need more than just a colour.

127846.q: What helps deaf people with videos on websites?
127846.e: Subtitles show what is said as text. That way deaf and hard of hearing people can understand the content.
127846.m: Subtitles make videos understandable for deaf people.

127847.q: Which Swiss law requires federal government websites to be accessible?
127847.e: The Disability Discrimination Act aims to prevent disadvantages for people with disabilities. It also obliges the federal government to make its online services accessible.
127847.m: In Switzerland, federal government websites must be accessible.

127848.q: Which HTML element starts a web form?
127848.e: All the input fields of a form are placed between <form> and </form>. The element also controls where the data is sent.
127848.m: A web form sits inside the form element.

127849.q: Which HTML element creates a single-line input field?
127849.e: <input type="text"> creates a single-line text field. With other types it becomes, for example, a date field or a button.
127849.m: Short entries are made with input.

127850.q: Which element is suitable for a longer text over several lines in a form?
127850.e: In a <textarea> you can write several lines, for example a message. Its size can be set with CSS or attributes.
127850.m: For long texts you use textarea.

127851.q: Which input type hides the characters you type behind dots?
127851.e: With type="password" the browser shows dots or asterisks instead of the characters. That way nobody looking at the screen can read along.
127851.m: Password fields have the type password.

127852.q: Which input type allows only exactly one choice out of several options?
127852.e: Radio buttons with the same name attribute form a group in which only one can be selected. With checkboxes you can tick several.
127852.m: With radio buttons you choose exactly one option.

127853.q: Which element links a label text to an input field?
127853.e: A <label> labels a field, and clicking on it activates the field. Screen readers connect the label to the field and read it out.
127853.m: Every input field should get a label.

127854.q: What does the required attribute do on an input field?
a: The field must be filled in
127854.e: With required, the browser only sends the form once the field is filled in. Otherwise a message appears.
127854.m: Required turns a field into a compulsory field.

127855.q: Which element creates a drop-down list?
127855.e: A <select> contains several <option> elements. You open the list and choose an entry, for example your canton.
127855.m: Drop-down lists are built with select and option.

127856.q: What can you do with JavaScript on a web page?
127856.e: With JavaScript a page reacts to clicks, checks entries or loads new content. HTML and CSS alone can hardly do that.

127857.q: Does JavaScript have anything to do with the programming language Java?
a: No, they are two different languages
Yes, it is the same language
Yes, JavaScript is an old version of Java
Yes, Java only runs with JavaScript
127857.e: Despite the similar name, Java and JavaScript are different languages. The name was chosen back then mainly for advertising reasons.
127857.m: Java and JavaScript are different languages despite their similar names.

127858.q: Which HTML element do you use to include JavaScript?
127858.e: JavaScript is placed in <script> elements or loaded from a file with <script src="file.js">. The browser then runs the code.
127858.m: JavaScript is included with the script element.

127859.q: What does console.log(2 + 3) show in the browser console?
127859.e: 2 and 3 are numbers, so JavaScript calculates 2 + 3 = 5. Only with text in quotation marks would the characters be joined together.
127859.m: JavaScript calculates with numbers quite normally.

127860.q: How do you write a one-line comment in JavaScript?
127860.e: The computer ignores everything after // up to the end of the line. Comments explain the code for humans.
127860.m: One-line comments in JavaScript start with two slashes.

127861.q: In modern JavaScript, which keyword creates a variable whose value is allowed to change?
127861.e: let number = 5; creates a variable that you can give a new value later. For values that should stay the same, you use const.
127861.m: Changeable variables are created with let.

127862.q: Where is JavaScript run on a normal web page?
127862.e: The browser has its own JavaScript engine that runs the code directly on the device. With Node.js, JavaScript can also run on servers.
127862.m: JavaScript usually runs directly in the browser.

127863.q: What does the comparison === mean in JavaScript?
a: Same value and same data type
127863.e: With ===, value and type must both match, so 5 === "5" is false. A single = on the other hand assigns a value.
127863.m: Three equals signs check value and type at the same time.

127864.q: In JavaScript, what do you call a function that runs when you click a button?
127864.e: An event handler reacts to events such as click or keydown. You connect it, for example, with addEventListener.
127864.m: JavaScript reacts to clicks with event handlers.

127865.q: You want to cross the road. What do you do first at the kerb?
127865.e: In Switzerland children learn: “Wait, look, listen, walk”. First you stop at the kerb, then you look and listen.

127866.q: What colour are zebra crossings in Switzerland?
127866.e: In Switzerland, zebra crossings are yellow. That makes them easy to see on the grey road.
127866.m: In Switzerland the zebra crossing is yellow.

127867.q: It is dark. What helps drivers see you better?
127867.e: Light colours and reflective strips shine in car headlights. That way the driver can see you from far away.
127867.m: Light and shiny means you are seen.

127868.q: Your ball rolls onto the road. What do you do?
127868.e: Children who run after a ball often forget about the cars. Stay at the side of the road and get help from a grown-up.
127868.m: No ball is as important as you.

127869.q: Mia's grandad falls over and does not wake up. Which number do you call?
127869.e: The number 144 calls the ambulance service. Paramedics help people who are ill or injured.

127870.q: What do you say on the phone when you call the emergency number?
a: Who you are, where you are and what has happened
127870.e: The helpers need to know where to come and what is going on. Stay calm and only hang up when they tell you to.
127870.m: Who, where, what: then help comes.

127871.q: Are you allowed to call the emergency number for fun?
a: No, only in a real emergency
Yes, if you hang up quickly
127871.e: If someone calls for fun, the line is busy. Then someone in real trouble might have to wait.
127871.m: An emergency call is not a game.

127872.q: What does the stop sign look like?
127872.e: The stop sign is red and has eight corners. Every vehicle must stop completely there.

127873.q: When is your bike helmet on properly?
a: It sits straight and the strap is fastened
It sits crooked at the back of your neck
127873.e: A helmet only protects you if it sits straight on your forehead and the chin strap is fastened. One finger should fit between the strap and your chin.
127873.m: Put it on straight, fasten the strap.

127874.q: Why does your bike have a bell?
127874.e: With the bell you show others that you are coming. That way pedestrians can make room for you.
127874.m: Ring ring means: watch out, here I come!

127875.q: Where does a banana skin go?
a: On the compost or in the green waste
127875.e: Banana skins are plant leftovers. On the compost they turn into new soil.

127876.q: Where do you take an empty jam jar?
127876.e: Glass can be melted down and made new. That is why it goes to the bottle bank.

127877.q: What do you do with a flat battery?
a: Take it to the collection box in a shop
127877.e: Batteries contain substances that harm nature. Every shop that sells batteries has a collection box.
127877.m: Flat batteries go back to the shop.

127878.q: You have an empty sweet wrapper in your hand. What do you do?
127878.e: Litter on the ground is bad for animals and looks ugly. If there is no bin, you take it home with you.

127879.q: What goes in the paper collection?
127879.e: Newspapers and exercise books are made of paper. New paper is made from waste paper.

127880.q: You meet your neighbour on the stairs. What do you say?
127880.e: In Switzerland people greet their neighbours in a friendly way with “Grüezi”. That makes living together nicer.

127881.q: It is late in the evening. Why do you play quietly now?
a: Because the neighbours want to sleep
Because otherwise the toys will break
Because you are never allowed to play in the evening
Because otherwise the lights go out
127881.e: In the evening and at night many people want to sleep. That is why everyone is quiet in the building then.
127881.m: At night the building is quiet.

127882.q: A stranger asks for your address in a chat. What do you do?
a: Give nothing away and show your parents
Send a photo of the house
127882.e: On the internet you can never be sure who is writing. Your address stays secret.

127883.q: Who is allowed to know your password?
127883.e: A password is like a key. Anyone who knows it can get into your account.

127884.q: You see a video online that frightens you. What do you do?
127884.e: If something frightens you, you can always talk about it. Grown-ups will help you.
127884.m: If something scares me, I tell someone.

127885.q: The bus stops. Who goes first?
127885.e: First people get off, then the others get on. That way there is no pushing.

127886.q: What do you need in the car to be safe?
a: A child seat and a seat belt
127886.e: In the car, children sit in a child seat and wear a seat belt. In an accident, this holds you in place.
127886.m: Belt up first, then drive off.

127887.q: A man you don't know wants to give you a lift in his car. What do you do?
127887.e: You never go with strangers, even if they are nice. Afterwards, tell your parents or your teacher.

127888.q: You find some matches. What do you do?
127888.e: A fire can start very quickly. That is why you give matches to a grown-up.

127889.q: Why is it dangerous to step into the road between parked cars?
a: Because the cars will drive off
Because it is too bright there
127889.e: Behind a car you are hidden from other drivers. It is better to cross where you can be seen clearly.
127889.m: If you are hidden, you are not seen.

127890.q: Where do pedestrians walk along a road?
a: In the middle of the road
127890.e: The pavement is the path for pedestrians next to the road. There you are protected from the cars.

127891.q: What does a triangular sign with a red border mean?
a: There is a cycle path here
127891.e: Triangular signs with a red border warn of danger. The picture in the middle shows what the danger is.
127891.m: A triangle with red means: be careful!

127892.q: A round blue sign shows a white bicycle. What does it mean?
a: There is a cycle path here
There is a bike shop here
127892.e: Round blue signs tell you what you must do. With a bike on it, the sign shows a cycle path.
127892.m: Blue and round with a bike: cycle path.

127893.q: A game on the tablet wants you to buy something. What do you do?
127893.e: Even in a game, a purchase like that costs real money. So always ask your parents first.
127893.m: Only buy things with your parents.

127894.q: You have lost your parents in the shopping centre. What do you do?
a: Ask a shop assistant at the till for help
127894.e: People who work in the shop are happy to help you. They can have your parents called over the loudspeaker.
127894.m: Lost? Ask someone who works there.

127895.q: You want to turn left on your bike. What do you do first?
a: Look behind you and stretch out your left arm
127895.e: With a hand signal you show others where you are going. Before that, look over your shoulder to check whether anyone is coming from behind.

127896.q: Which lights does a bike need at night?
a: White at the front, red at the back
Red at the front, white at the back
Blue at the front and back
Just one light on the helmet
127896.e: At night and when it is hard to see, a bike must have a white light at the front and a red light at the back. That way others can see which way you are going.
127896.m: White to the front, red to the back.

127897.q: In Switzerland, who may ride a bike on the pavement if there is no cycle path?
127897.e: Since 2021, children up to 12 may ride on the pavement if there is no cycle path or cycle lane. But they must be considerate towards pedestrians.
127897.m: Up to 12 on the pavement, but pedestrians first.

127898.q: At a crossroads with no sign and no traffic lights, who has right of way?
127898.e: Unless a sign says otherwise, in Switzerland traffic from the right has right of way. This applies to cyclists too.

127899.q: You are cycling towards a roundabout. Who has right of way?
a: Whoever is already on the roundabout
127899.e: On a roundabout, the vehicles already on it have right of way. Anyone who wants to join must wait.
127899.m: On a roundabout, whoever is on it goes first.

127900.q: In Switzerland, when do you usually buy your ticket for the train or bus?
a: Only if there is a ticket check
127900.e: On almost all trains, trams and buses you must have your ticket before the journey. Anyone travelling without a ticket pays a surcharge.
127900.m: First the ticket, then get on.

127901.q: What does a Half Fare travelcard give you?
a: Most tickets cost about half price
You can always travel first class
127901.e: With the Half Fare travelcard you pay about half price for most public transport tickets. It is worth it for people who travel often.

127902.q: What can you do with a GA travelcard?
a: Travel freely on almost all Swiss public transport
Only take the bus in one city
127902.e: The GA is valid on almost all trains, buses, trams and many boats in Switzerland. You can travel as often as you like with it.
127902.m: With the GA you can travel almost anywhere.

127903.q: From what age do children need their own train ticket?
127903.e: Children under 6 travel free when accompanied. From 6 to 16 they usually pay a reduced child fare.

127904.q: Luca is on the tram without a valid ticket. What happens if there is a ticket check?
a: He has to pay a surcharge
127904.e: Anyone caught without a valid ticket pays the fare plus a surcharge. That costs more than a ticket.

a: Besides the password you also need a code
You have two passwords on a piece of paper
You log in twice the same way
127905.e: When logging in, you also need a code, for example from an app or by text message. That way a thief cannot get into the account with just the password.
127905.m: Two locks are safer than one.

127906.q: You get a text: “Parcel waiting, pay 2 francs using this link.” What do you do?
a: Don't click and delete the text
127906.e: Messages like this are often a scam, called phishing. The scammers want your data or your money.

127907.q: Why is a screen lock code on your phone important?
a: So strangers cannot get at your data
127907.e: Without a lock, anyone who finds your phone can see your photos and messages. A code protects your data.

127908.q: Nora keeps being insulted in a class chat. What helps most?
a: Take screenshots and show a trusted adult
Quietly delete everything and say nothing
127908.e: Screenshots are evidence. A trusted adult can help make the bullying stop. You can also block and report the bullies.

127909.q: Which number can children and young people in Switzerland call when they are worried?
127909.e: On 147, Pro Juventute offers advice for children and young people day and night. It is free and confidential.

127910.q: You want to post a photo of your friend online. What must you do?
a: Make the photo black and white
127910.e: Everyone can decide for themselves whether a photo of them is published. This is called the right to your own image.

127911.q: A person is unconscious but breathing normally. How do you position them?
a: On their front with a pillow
On their back with legs raised
127911.e: In the recovery position the airway stays clear, because saliva or vomit can run out. Then call 144 and keep watching the person.

127912.q: You burn your hand on the oven. What is the right thing to do?
127912.e: Tap water cools the skin and eases the pain. Cool it for about 10 to 20 minutes, and not with ice-cold water.
127912.m: Burnt? Hold it under the water!

127913.q: What do you do when you have a nosebleed?
a: Lean your head forward and pinch your nose
127913.e: With your head forward, the blood does not run into your throat. A cold cloth on the back of your neck can also help.

127914.q: What is an AED, a defibrillator, used for?
127914.e: An AED gives the heart an electric shock so that it beats properly again. The device tells you out loud what to do.

127915.q: Oil is burning in the pan. What must you never do?
a: Put a fire blanket over it
127915.e: Water turns to steam instantly in hot oil and sprays burning fat everywhere. A lid or fire blanket smothers the fire.
127915.m: Never put out a fat fire with water.

127916.q: There is a fire in a block of flats. Why should you not use the lift?
a: It can get stuck and fill with smoke
It costs money in an emergency
127916.e: In a fire the power can fail and the lift shaft can fill with smoke. You escape by the stairs.
127916.m: In a fire, always use the stairs.

127917.q: Why is it a good idea to have a smoke alarm at home?
a: It wakes you with a loud sound if there is smoke
It puts out the fire itself
127917.e: When you are asleep you cannot smell smoke. The smoke alarm beeps loudly so you can escape in time.

127918.q: Why do people sort waste glass by colour?
a: Because each colour is made into the same glass again
Because otherwise it will not melt
127918.e: Clear, green and brown glass are melted down separately. That way new glass of the same colour is made.
127918.m: Clear, green, brown: each on its own.

127919.q: Where can you take an old hairdryer free of charge in Switzerland?
a: To a shop that sells such appliances
127919.e: Shops must take back old electrical appliances free of charge. The recycling has already been paid for in the price.
127919.m: Old appliances go back to the shop.

127920.q: Why is it worth collecting aluminium cans?
a: Recycling uses much less energy than making new aluminium
The cans are filled with drinks again
Otherwise aluminium rots on the compost
127920.e: Making new aluminium takes a lot of electricity. Melting down old aluminium saves most of it.

127921.q: Why must boxes and bikes not be left standing in the stairwell?
a: Because it is an escape route
Because otherwise the lift will not work
Because otherwise it gets too cold
127921.e: In a fire or emergency, everyone must be able to escape quickly through the stairwell. The fire brigade needs space too.

127922.q: From what time do quiet hours at night start in many Swiss buildings?
127922.e: The exact times are in the house rules or the municipality's regulations. Quiet hours often run from 10 pm to 6 or 7 am.
127922.m: From ten o'clock it is quiet.

127923.q: The tenancy agreement does not mention any additional costs. What applies then?
a: They are included in the rent
The landlord can charge as much as he likes
The tenant pays all the costs of the building
127923.e: A landlord may only charge additional costs if they are listed individually in the agreement. Otherwise they count as included in the rent.
127923.m: Whatever is not in the agreement is included.

127924.q: Sara pays her additional costs “on account” every month. What does that mean?
a: They are settled at the end of the year, with an extra payment or a refund
The amount is fixed and final
The landlord gives her the amount as a gift
127924.e: On account means paying in advance. The real costs are settled in the yearly statement.
127924.m: On account is a payment in advance, settled later.

127925.q: Where must a rental deposit paid in money be kept?
a: In a blocked account in the tenant's name
127925.e: The law requires a bank account or deposit in the tenant's name. The landlord cannot simply use it himself.
127925.m: The deposit belongs in an account in your name.

127926.q: Why is a handover report important when you move in?
a: It registers you with the municipality
127926.e: Whatever is in the report was already broken before. That way you do not have to pay for someone else's damage when you move out.
127926.m: Writing down defects protects you when you move out.

127927.q: After moving in, the tap drips all the time. What is the best way to report it?
a: Not at all, have it repaired yourself
Only mention it when moving out
127927.e: A written report counts as proof. The landlord must repair defects that are not part of the tenant's minor maintenance.

127928.q: Can you simply sublet your rented flat?
127928.e: Subletting requires the landlord's consent. However, he may only refuse it for certain reasons, for example if the rent charged is excessive.
127928.m: Sublet only with the landlord's yes.

127929.q: What must a landlord use to give notice on a flat?
127929.e: If the landlord gives notice, a form approved by the canton is required. Otherwise the notice is void.
127929.m: A landlord's notice only counts on the official form.

127930.q: What happens if you are underinsured with household contents insurance?
a: The insurance pays less if there is a claim
127930.e: If the contents are worth more than the sum insured, the insurer reduces the payment. That is why you should check the sum regularly.
127930.m: Insured too low means too little money.

127931.q: Your bike is stolen outside the station. Which insurance usually helps?
a: Household contents insurance with extra cover for theft away from home
127931.e: Theft outside the home is often an extra option in household contents insurance. You report the theft to the police first.
127931.m: Stolen bike: household contents insurance with extra cover.

127932.q: Tim scratches a parked car with his bike. Who usually pays for the damage?
a: The owner of the car himself
127932.e: The Swiss bicycle insurance sticker was abolished in 2012. Damage you cause with your bike is covered by private liability insurance.
127932.m: Bike damage is paid by private liability insurance.

127933.q: Which insurance is compulsory for every car in Switzerland?
127933.e: Without motor vehicle liability insurance you get no number plates. It pays for damage you cause to others.
127933.m: No liability insurance, no number plates.

127934.q: What does a mail forwarding order with Swiss Post do?
a: Letters go to the new address for a certain time
127934.e: After a move, Swiss Post forwards letters to the new address for a period you choose. You should still tell everyone your new address.
127934.m: Forwarding: the post finds you at your new address.

127935.q: Lea is moving to a different municipality. Where does she deregister?
a: With the federal government in Bern
127935.e: Anyone moving away deregisters with the residents' registration office of the old municipality. In the new municipality you register within the deadline.
127935.m: Deregister in the old municipality, register in the new one.

127936.q: How long is the probation period after passing the driving test in Switzerland?
127936.e: After passing the test you receive a probationary driving licence for 3 years. For serious offences it can be extended or cancelled.

127937.q: What alcohol limit applies to new drivers with a probationary licence?
127937.e: For new drivers and learners there is practically a ban on alcohol, with a limit of 0.1 per mille. For other drivers the limit is 0.5 per mille.

127938.q: What do you need before you can apply for a learner's permit for a car?
127938.e: The first aid course is a requirement for applying for the learner's permit. There you learn first aid on the road.
127938.m: First aid first, then the learner's permit.

127939.q: From what age can you ride a moped with category M?
127939.e: At 14 you can get a category M licence after a theory test. Wearing a helmet is compulsory on a moped.

127940.q: What is the maximum speed a moped is built to reach?
127940.e: A moped is built so that it reaches at most 30 km/h. Faster vehicles need a different licence category.

127941.q: Under the Data Protection Act, what can you ask a company for?
a: Information about what data it holds about you
127941.e: Everyone has a right to information about their own personal data. The information is usually free of charge.
127941.m: I have the right to know what is stored about me.

127942.q: Who supervises data protection at federal level in Switzerland?
a: The Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner
127942.e: The FDPIC supervises federal offices and private companies in matters of data protection. It can open investigations and advises the public.
127942.m: The FDPIC keeps watch over data.

127943.q: What should you do with out-of-date medicines?
a: Take them back to the chemist
127943.e: Medicines must not go into the waste water or on the compost. Chemists and pharmacies take them back and dispose of them properly.
127943.m: Old medicines go back to the chemist.

127944.q: Where is the best place to keep the medicine cabinet?
a: Dry, cool and out of children's reach
On the floor of the damp bathroom
127944.e: Damp and heat can spoil medicines. Small children must not be able to get at medicines.

127945.q: A household has neither a television nor a radio. Does it have to pay the media licence fee?
a: Yes, it basically applies to every household
127945.e: Since 2019 the fee has been linked to the household, not to devices. People receiving supplementary benefits, for example, can be exempted.

127946.q: How long can you collect a registered letter after receiving a collection notice?
127946.e: Swiss Post keeps registered items for 7 days. For letters from authorities, a letter often counts as delivered on the last day of this period.
127946.m: Registered post: seven days to collect.

127947.q: What is the difference between A Post and B Post?
a: A Post arrives faster and costs more
B Post is only for parcels
You have to collect B Post yourself
127947.e: A Post letters usually arrive the next working day. B Post is cheaper but takes a few working days longer.
127947.m: A is fast, B is cheap.

127948.q: You have lost your identity card. What must you do?
a: Report the loss to the police
Nothing, it will soon be invalid
127948.e: A lost identity document must be reported to the police. It is then blocked in the search system so that nobody can misuse it.
127948.m: ID gone? Go to the police.

127949.q: What does a bank mainly do?
a: It looks after money and lends money
127949.e: A bank looks after the money of lots of people. It also lends money, for example for a house.

127950.q: Who helps you at the counter in the bank?
a: A police officer with a dog
127950.e: Bank clerks work at the counter. They answer questions and help you pay in or withdraw money.
127950.m: At the bank counter, experts help you.

127951.q: What do you call a person who keeps their money at a bank?
127951.e: Anyone who has an account at a bank is a customer there.
127951.m: If you have an account, you are a customer of the bank.

127952.q: The Meier family wants to buy a house but does not have enough money. What can the bank do?
127952.e: Banks lend money. Later you must pay it back, and usually a bit more than you received.
127952.m: Borrowed money has to be paid back.

127953.q: What is the thick, strong cupboard in the bank for money and valuables called?
127953.e: A safe has thick steel walls and a strong lock. Valuable things are well protected inside.
127953.m: Valuables are safe in the safe.

127954.q: Where does the bank get the money it lends?
a: From the people who put money in their accounts
The Federal Council gives it to them
127954.e: Lots of people put money in their accounts. The bank can lend some of it to others. You still get your money back when you need it.
127954.m: The bank works with savers' money.

a: A place at the bank where your money is recorded
127955.e: In an account, the bank writes down how much money belongs to you. The money is not kept in its own box with your name on.
127955.m: Your account shows how much money belongs to you.

127956.q: Who can open an account for a child up to the age of 9?
a: The parents together with the child
127956.e: Young children need their parents or other guardians to open an account. The parents help and keep an eye on it.
127956.m: For young children, the parents open the account.

127957.q: What does the account balance show?
a: How much money is in the account right now
127957.e: The account balance tells you how much money you have in your account at the moment.
127957.m: The balance shows your money in the account.

127958.q: Mia has 20 francs in her account. She pays in 10 francs. How much does she have now?
127958.e: 20 francs and 10 francs make 30 francs together. Paying in makes the balance bigger.

127959.q: Tim has 50 francs in his account. He withdraws 20 francs. How much is left?
127959.e: 50 francs minus 20 francs is 30 francs. Withdrawing makes the balance smaller.

127960.q: Why does every account have its own number?
a: So the money arrives in the right account
So it can be drawn in the lottery
127960.e: Every account has its own number, the IBAN. That way the bank knows exactly where the money belongs.
127960.m: Every account has its own number.

127961.q: Does the money in your account belong to the bank?
a: Yes, it belongs to the bank
127961.e: The bank only looks after your money. It stays your money and you can take it out again.
127961.m: Your money in the account stays your money.

127962.q: What is a children's or youth account?
a: An account made especially for young people
An account that only works on Sundays
127962.e: Many banks have accounts for children and young people. They help you learn how to handle money.
127962.m: Children can have their own account too.

127963.q: Granny gives Lea 100 francs for her birthday. Lea wants to buy a bike later. Where should the money go?
a: Spend it on sweets straight away
Leave it lying around in her bedroom
Put it in her school desk
127963.e: In the savings account the money is kept safe. When Lea has saved enough, she can buy the bike.
127963.m: For a big goal, use your savings account.

a: A small tin or figure for collecting money
127964.e: In a money box you collect coins and notes at home. That way you can see your savings grow.
127964.m: You collect your money in a money box.

127965.q: Which animal is often the shape of a money box?
127965.e: The piggy bank is very well known. It has a slot on top for the coins.
127965.m: The piggy bank loves eating coins.

127966.q: Why does a money box have a slot on top?
a: So you can put coins and notes in
So you can hang it up
127966.e: You put the money in through the slot. Getting it out is not so easy, which helps you save.
127966.m: Easy to put in, hard to take out.

127967.q: Your money box is full. Where can you take the money so it is kept safe?
a: To the bank, into your savings account
127967.e: When the money box is full, you can take the money to the bank with your parents. There it goes into your account.
127967.m: Full money box? Off to the bank.

127968.q: Noah wants a game that costs 30 francs. He saves 5 francs every week. How many weeks does he need?
127968.e: 5 francs times 6 weeks is 30 francs. With patience, Noah reaches his goal.
127968.m: Small amounts grow big over time.

127969.q: What is the money called that children get regularly from their parents?
127969.e: Many children get pocket money every week or every month. With it they learn to handle money themselves.
127969.m: With pocket money you learn to count and save.

127970.q: Sara gets 4 francs pocket money. She spends 1 franc and saves the rest. How much does she save?
127970.e: 4 francs minus 1 franc is 3 francs. Sara can put them in her money box.
127970.m: What you don't spend, you can save.

a: First think about whether you really need something
Buy everything you see straight away
Empty the money box every day
Always carry money in your pocket
127971.e: Before you buy something, ask yourself: do I really need this? That way more money is left over.

127972.q: What do you really need to live?
127972.e: Every person needs food and drink. Toys are nice, but you can live without them.
127972.m: First what you need, then what is nice.

127973.q: What can you do at a cash machine?
127973.e: At the cash machine you put in your bank card and type your PIN. Then it gives out money from your account.
127973.m: At the cash machine you get cash.

127974.q: What do you need to get money from a cash machine?
a: Your bank card and your PIN
127974.e: The cash machine recognises you by your card. With your secret PIN you show that the card belongs to you.

127975.q: Where does the money from the cash machine come from?
a: It is a present from the bank
127975.e: The money is taken from your account. If there is nothing in the account, there is no money either.
127975.m: The cash machine only gives what is in your account.

127976.q: Someone is standing very close behind you at the cash machine. What do you do?
a: Cover the PIN with your hand or wait
Write the PIN on the screen
127976.e: Nobody should see which numbers you type. Cover the keys with your hand or ask them to step back.
127976.m: Cover the keys while you type.

127977.q: What should you not forget after withdrawing money?
a: To take your card and the money
To say the PIN out loud
To write the PIN on a note
To put the receipt into the machine
127977.e: Always take the card first and then the money. Only then do you walk away.
127977.m: Always take your card and money.

127978.q: Where do you often find a cash machine in Switzerland?
a: At a bank or at the railway station
127978.e: Cash machines are in lots of places: at banks, at railway stations or in shopping centres.
127978.m: Cash machines are where lots of people are.

127979.q: The cash machine keeps your card. What do you do?
a: Just go home and say nothing
127979.e: If the card stays in the machine, your parents or the bank must be told quickly. They know what to do.
127979.m: Problem with your card? Tell someone straight away.

a: A secret number for your card
127980.e: The PIN is a secret number. Only you know it, so nobody else can use your card.

127981.q: Your best friend asks for your PIN. What do you say?
a: I'll write it down for you
I'll tell everyone in the class
127981.e: You never give away your PIN, not even to good friends. That way your money stays protected.
127981.m: Only one person knows the PIN: you.

127982.q: Where is the best place to keep your PIN?
a: On a note in your purse
On a sticker on your phone
127982.e: Otherwise anyone who finds the card and the note could take money. It is best to learn your PIN by heart.
127982.m: Never write your PIN on the card.

127983.q: You have lost your bank card. What do you do first?
a: Tell your parents straight away so the card can be blocked
127983.e: A lost card must be blocked quickly. Then nobody else can pay with it.
127983.m: Card gone? Have it blocked at once.

127984.q: May a stranger borrow your bank card?
a: No, the card belongs only to you
Yes, if he brings it back
127984.e: Your card is only for you. Never give it to a stranger.

127985.q: Which PIN is the worst, because it is easy to guess?
127985.e: Thieves try numbers like 1234 or 0000 first. A good PIN has no simple pattern.
127985.m: A good PIN is not a simple pattern.

127986.q: What is a bank card usually made of?
127986.e: Bank cards are made of strong plastic. They have a small chip that stores important data.
127986.m: A bank card is made of plastic with a chip.

127987.q: What is the small gold or silver part on a bank card?
a: A chip with the card's data
127987.e: The chip stores the card's data. Card readers in shops or at cash machines can read it.
127987.m: The chip is the card's brain.

127988.q: What is the best way to treat your bank card?
a: Keep it in your purse and don't bend it
Carry it loose in your school bag
Give it to your friends to play with
127988.e: A bent or broken card might not work any more. Keep it in your purse or wallet.
127988.m: Take good care of your card.

127989.q: How many digits does a bank card PIN often have?
127989.e: A PIN usually has 4 or 6 digits. That makes it easy to remember.
127989.m: A PIN is short but secret.

a: Taking money out of your account
127990.e: When you pay in, money goes into your account. Your balance gets bigger.
127990.m: Paying in: money goes into the account.

a: Taking money out of your account
127991.e: When you withdraw, you take money out of your account, for example at a cash machine. Your balance gets smaller.
127991.m: Withdrawing: money comes out of the account.

127992.q: Where can you pay cash into an account?
a: At the bank counter or a deposit machine
127992.e: You can hand in cash at the counter or pay it in at special machines. Then it goes into your account.
127992.m: You pay in cash at the bank.

127993.q: Ben has 10 francs in his account and wants to withdraw 50 francs. What happens?
a: It doesn't work, because there is not enough money
127993.e: You can only withdraw what is in the account. The account cannot give out more than it holds.
127993.m: You can only take out what is there.

127994.q: Lars pays in 5 francs, then another 5 francs. Before that, the account was empty. How much is in it?
127994.e: 5 and 5 make 10. Every payment in makes the balance bigger.
127994.m: Lots of small payments add up to a lot.

a: A slip of paper showing what was paid
127995.e: A receipt shows how much money was paid or paid in. It is proof.

127996.q: What is the small amount of money the bank sometimes gives you when your money stays in a savings account for a long time?
127996.e: The bank sometimes pays you a small amount for keeping your money there. This is called interest.
127996.m: Interest is a small thank you for saving.

127997.q: Your parents borrow money from the bank. Who has to pay interest?
127997.e: Whoever borrows money from the bank later pays back more than they received. The extra is the interest.

127998.q: Leonie has saved 100 francs. At the end of the year there are 101 francs in her account. Where does the extra franc come from?
a: It is interest from the bank
127998.e: The bank has paid Leonie interest. That is a small amount for the money she saved.
127998.m: Saved money can grow a little.

127999.q: Which statement about interest on a savings account is true?
a: It is often only a small amount
It makes you rich straight away
127999.e: Interest on a savings account is usually small. But over many years it can add up.
127999.m: Interest is small, but over time it counts.

128000.q: What happens with interest if you keep your money in a money box at home?
128000.e: Only the bank can pay interest. In the money box, the money stays exactly the same.
128000.m: Money does not grow in a money box.

a: Coins and notes you can touch
128001.e: Cash means coins and banknotes. You can hold them in your hand and count them.

128002.q: What can you pay with in a shop?
128002.e: In a shop you pay with coins and notes or with a card. Sometimes you can use your phone too.

128003.q: What is one advantage of cash?
a: You can see exactly how much money you have left
You can pay with it in any country
128003.e: With cash in your purse you can see at once how much is left. That helps you not to spend too much.
128003.m: Cash shows you clearly what you have.

128004.q: What happens when you pay with your bank card in a shop?
a: The money is taken from your account
You get the things for free
The card goes empty and breaks
128004.e: When you pay by card, the bank takes the money from your account and gives it to the shop.
128004.m: Card money is real money too.

128005.q: What is a disadvantage of only paying by card?
a: You notice less how much you are spending
You can only buy small things
You have to count the coins yourself
128005.e: With a card the money flows away invisibly. That is why it is easier to lose track.

128006.q: What do you keep coins, notes and cards in when you are out?
a: In a PE bag with no zip
128006.e: A purse or wallet keeps your money and your card together. That way nothing gets lost.
128006.m: Money belongs in a purse or wallet.

128007.q: You pay for an ice cream costing 3 francs with a 5-franc coin. How much change do you get?
128007.e: 5 francs minus 3 francs is 2 francs. That is your change.

128008.q: What does contactless payment by card mean?
a: Just holding the card briefly to the reader
Putting the card into the reader
Giving the card to the shop assistant
128008.e: For small amounts you hold the card briefly against the card reader. For larger amounts you usually have to enter your PIN.

128009.q: Which coin has the highest value in Switzerland?
128009.e: The five-franc coin, or Fünfliber, has the highest value. It is also the biggest and heaviest Swiss coin.
128009.m: The five-franc coin is the biggest coin.

128011.q: Which Swiss coin is golden yellow?
128011.e: The 5-centime coin shines golden yellow. The other coins are silvery.

128012.q: What is the 5-franc coin often called in Switzerland?
128012.e: Fünfliber is an old, popular name for the 5-franc coin.

128013.q: Which Swiss banknote has the lowest value?
128013.e: The smallest banknote is the 10-franc note. For 5 francs there is a coin.
128013.m: The smallest note is the 10-franc note.

128014.q: Which Swiss banknote has the highest value?
128014.e: The biggest note is the 1000-franc note. It is purple. There is no 500-franc note in Switzerland.

128015.e: There are notes of 10, 20, 50, 100, 200 and 1000 francs. The 200-franc note is brown.

128016.q: How many different banknotes are there in Switzerland?

128017.e: 50 centimes and 50 centimes make 100 centimes, which is 1 franc.

128018.e: 5 times 20 centimes is 100 centimes, which is 1 franc.

128019.e: 10 times 10 centimes is 100 centimes, which is 1 franc.

128020.q: How many 10-franc notes are worth the same as a 100-franc note?

128021.q: How many 20-franc notes are worth the same as a 100-franc note?

128022.q: Which is worth more: a 2-franc coin or four 50-centime coins?
128022.e: Four times 50 centimes is 200 centimes, which is 2 francs. Both are the same.
128022.m: Same amount of money, different coins.

128023.q: You have a 1-franc coin and a 50-centime coin. How much money is that?
128023.e: 1 franc and 50 centimes together make 1 franc 50 centimes.
128023.m: Add up the francs and the centimes.

128024.q: Which woman can you see on the 1-franc coin?
128024.e: The standing woman on the coin is Helvetia. She is a symbol of Switzerland.

a: Copied money that is not real
128025.e: Counterfeit money is copied and illegal. Real notes have special security features.
128025.m: Counterfeit money is not real money.

128026.q: Why do banknotes glitter and shimmer in some places?
a: To make them hard to copy
To make them glow in the dark
So you can find them faster in your purse
128026.e: Glittering parts and special pictures are security features. They make it hard to forge notes.

128027.q: What do you pay with when you use TWINT?
128027.e: TWINT is an app on your phone. You can use it to pay in shops or send money to other people.

128028.q: Where does the money come from when you pay with TWINT?
128028.e: TWINT is linked to a bank account. The money is taken from there.
128028.m: TWINT money is real money too.

128029.q: What can you do with TWINT?
128029.e: With TWINT you can send money to another person who has TWINT, for example for a shared present.
128029.m: With TWINT you can pass money on quickly.

128030.q: How do you often pay with TWINT in a shop?
a: You scan a code with your phone
128030.e: In shops the till often shows a QR code. You scan it with the TWINT app and confirm the amount.

128031.q: Who should be there when a child uses TWINT for the first time?
128031.e: The parents help set it up and explain how to pay safely.
128031.m: Try out new money apps with your parents.

128032.q: Someone you don't know sends you a TWINT request for money. What do you do?
a: Decline it and show your parents
128032.e: You only pay people you know, and when you know what for. With strangers, always ask your parents.
128032.m: Unknown request? Don't pay, ask your parents.

128033.q: Why does the TWINT app have a code or fingerprint to unlock it?
a: So that only you can pay with it
To make the phone look nicer
128033.e: The code protects your money. If someone takes your phone, they cannot pay without the code.
128033.m: The app code protects your money.

128034.q: Your purse has gone. What is a good thing to do?
128034.e: If there was a card in the purse, it must be blocked quickly. Your parents will help you.

128035.q: On the phone, someone says they are from the bank and asks for your PIN. What do you do?
a: Give nothing away and hang up
128035.e: A real bank never asks for your PIN. Hang up and tell your parents.
128035.m: The bank never asks for your PIN.

128036.q: You find a purse in the street. What do you do?
a: Hand it in, for example at the lost property office or the police
128036.e: Things you find belong to someone else. Hand it in with a grown-up at the lost property office or the police.
128036.m: You hand in things you find.

128037.q: Where is your purse safest on the bus?
a: In a closed bag close to your body
Open on the seat next to you
Hanging on the outside of your rucksack
In your hand, high in the air
128037.e: In a closed bag close to you, nobody can simply take it.
128037.m: Carry money close to your body.

128039.q: Something strange is stuck onto the cash machine. What do you do?
a: Not put your card in and tell a grown-up
Pull the thing off and take it
128039.e: Sometimes fraudsters stick devices onto cash machines. If something looks strange, don't use the machine.

128040.q: Lena is 12 and would like her own account. What is usually best for her?
a: A youth account with low or no fees
A mortgage with a fixed rate
An account with a high credit limit
128040.e: Banks offer special accounts for children and young people. They are often free of fees and cannot go overdrawn.

128041.q: What usually happens if you try to spend more than is in a youth account?
a: The bank gives you the missing amount
128041.e: Youth accounts usually cannot be overdrawn. That way young people cannot get into debt on their account.
128041.m: No money in it, no payment.

128042.q: What often happens to a youth account when you get older and reach the age limit?
a: It is turned into a normal personal account
It is closed and the money is lost
It goes to the National Bank
It turns into a piggy bank
128042.e: Youth accounts only apply up to a certain age. After that the account is usually turned into a personal account with different conditions.
128042.m: The account grows up with you.

128043.q: What is a personal current account mainly for?
128043.e: For example, your wages go into your current account, and you pay bills and shopping from it. A savings account is better for saving.
128043.m: Current account for paying, savings account for saving.

128044.q: Which statement about a savings account is usually true?
a: You cannot withdraw as much as you like at once
You get a free credit card with it
You pay all your bills from it
128044.e: Many savings accounts have limits on how much you can withdraw per month without giving notice. In return, the interest is often a bit higher than on a current account.
128044.m: Savings account: let the money rest.

128045.q: Nico puts 20 francs into his savings account every month. How much has he saved after one year, without interest?
128045.e: A year has 12 months. 12 times 20 francs makes 240 francs.
128045.m: Small amounts add up to big ones.

128046.q: Why is it worth putting money into a savings account rather than a piggy bank?
a: It is safer and can earn interest
The bank adds 100 francs every year
You can withdraw unlimited amounts at any time
You never have to think about the money again
128046.e: In a savings account the money is protected against theft and loss. The bank also pays interest, depending on interest rates.
128046.m: Money in the bank does a little work too.

128047.q: Mia pays in a shop with her debit card. When is the money taken from her account?
a: Straight away or within a few days
128047.e: With a debit card the amount is taken directly from your own account. So you can only spend what is there.
128047.m: Debit: the money goes straight away.

128048.q: How do you normally pay for shopping done with a credit card?
a: Not at all, the bank covers it
Each purchase separately at the counter
128048.e: With a credit card, the company collects all your purchases and sends a bill once a month. You must pay it on time.
128048.m: Credit means: buy first, pay later.

128049.q: What happens if you only pay part of your credit card bill?
a: High interest is charged on the rest
The rest is automatically let off
The card becomes twice as big
128049.e: If you only pay part, the rest counts as a loan. Credit card companies charge high interest on it.
128049.m: Always pay off your credit card in full.

a: A card you first have to top up with money
A card you can pay with without limit
A card only for cash machines abroad
A card that never has a PIN
128050.e: Prepaid means “paid in advance”. You can only spend as much as you have loaded onto it.

128051.q: From what age do people in Switzerland usually get a real credit card?
a: From the first day of school
128051.e: For a credit card you must be an adult, and the bank checks your income. Younger people get at most a prepaid or debit card.

128052.q: What does the wave symbol on a bank card mean?
a: The card only works at the seaside
128052.e: With the wave symbol you just hold the card briefly against the payment terminal. For small amounts you often don't need a PIN.

128053.q: Why do you still have to enter your PIN now and then when paying contactless?
a: For protection in case the card has been stolen
So the card is topped up again
So the shop pays lower fees
128053.e: Above a certain amount or after several payments, the terminal asks for the PIN. That way a thief cannot spend as much as they like.
128053.m: The PIN is the card's lock.

128054.q: Leon has lost his bank card. What should he do straight away?
a: Have the card blocked by the bank
Wait a week to see if it turns up
Post the PIN on social media
Open a new account at another bank
128054.e: You should have a lost card blocked at once, by phone or in the app. Then nobody can pay with it any more.
128054.m: Card gone? Block it at once!

128055.q: What is the three-digit number on the back of many cards?
a: A security code for internet payments
The number of purchases per day
128055.e: The security code, often called CVV, is needed when buying online. Only enter it in secure shops and never give it to strangers on the phone.
128055.m: The back of the card stays secret.

a: A random number that has nothing to do with you
128056.e: Thieves can easily guess simple sequences and dates of birth. A random PIN is much harder to crack.

128057.q: What usually happens if you enter the wrong PIN three times?
a: The card gives out more money
Nothing, you can keep trying for ever
128057.e: After several wrong attempts, the bank blocks the card. That way a thief cannot simply try out PINs.

128058.q: Why do you cover the keypad with your hand when typing your PIN?
a: So nobody can spy on your PIN
128058.e: Thieves sometimes look over your shoulder or film secretly. With your hand covering the keys, your PIN stays secret.
128058.m: Hand over the keys, PIN stays secret.

128059.q: Is it all right to write your PIN on the card so you don't forget it?
a: No, otherwise a finder can use the card at once
Yes, if the card is new
128059.e: If the PIN is on the card, a thief has everything they need. You then often have to pay for any loss yourself.
128059.m: PIN in your head, not on the card.

128060.e: The PIN is personal. Even the bank never asks for it, neither on the phone nor by email.
128060.m: My PIN belongs only to me.

128061.q: What should you do if a cash machine looks odd, for example with a loose card slot?
a: Not use it and inform the bank
Quickly put your card in anyway
128061.e: Fraudsters sometimes fit devices to cash machines that copy card data. This is called skimming.

128062.q: What is the trick called where fraudsters copy card data at a cash machine?
128062.e: With skimming, a reader is fitted over the card slot, often with a mini camera for the PIN. This is used to make fake cards.

128063.q: Why can withdrawing money from another bank's cash machine cost something?
a: Some banks charge a fee for it
Because the money there is older
Because other machines only give coins
Because you get twice as much there
128063.e: At your own bank, withdrawing is usually free. At other machines or abroad, fees may apply.
128063.m: Using your own bank's machine saves fees.

128064.q: What should you do first after withdrawing money?
a: Put your card and money away at once
Count the money out loud in front of everyone
Leave the card in the machine
Take a photo of the PIN
128064.e: Put your card and cash away safely straight away. Counting for ages attracts thieves.

128065.q: On TWINT, what are you usually found by when someone wants to send you money?
128065.e: On TWINT you can send money to contacts in your phone book. The mobile number is used to identify you.
128065.m: TWINT knows you by your mobile number.

128067.q: Jana paid for everyone's cinema tickets. How can she get the money back from her friends with TWINT?
a: She has to send a bill by post
She has to go to the National Bank
128067.e: In TWINT you can request money from contacts. Your friends just have to confirm the request.

128068.q: A stranger asks you on TWINT to confirm a payment request so that you will “receive money”. What is true?
a: Confirming sends your money away, so decline
It is a safe game rule
You have to give away your PIN for it
128068.e: With a payment request, you pay if you confirm. Fraudsters use this trick on selling platforms.

128069.q: What should the TWINT app be protected with?
a: Nothing at all, for faster paying
Your pet's name on the screen
128069.e: Anyone who finds the phone should not be able to simply send money. That is why the app needs a code or fingerprint.

128070.q: What can you do with online banking, for example?
a: See your balance and pay bills
Take money from other people's accounts
128070.e: With online banking you do your banking on a computer or phone. You can see account activity and make payments.
128070.m: Online banking: the bank in your pocket.

128071.q: What should you always do after using online banking?
a: Write down the password and leave it lying around
128071.e: Logging out ends the session. Otherwise someone else could carry on using it on the same device.

128072.q: What is the safest way to open online banking?
a: Type the address yourself or use the official app
Click a link in an unknown email
Through an advert in a game
Through a link in a text message
128072.e: Links in messages can lead to fake websites. If you type the address yourself, you safely reach the real bank.
128072.m: Type it yourself instead of clicking.

128073.q: Why should you not do online banking on a public computer?
a: Other people's devices can read your data
Because public computers are too slow
Because your account will then be deleted
Because only games run on them
128073.e: Other devices could have malware installed that records passwords. It is better to do your banking on your own device.
128073.m: Do your banking only on your own device.

a: A bill that comes straight into your online banking
A game run by the National Bank
128074.e: With eBill you receive bills digitally in your online banking. You check them and approve payment with one click.

128075.q: What do you need an IBAN for?
a: So that money reaches the right account
To buy chewing gum at the kiosk
As a password for online banking
128075.e: The IBAN is the international account number. Anyone who wants to transfer money to you needs your IBAN.

128076.q: How many characters does a Swiss IBAN have?
128076.e: A Swiss IBAN has 21 characters: CH, two check digits, the bank's number and the account number.

128077.q: Is it all right to give out your IBAN so that you can receive money?
a: Yes, nobody can withdraw money with it
No, otherwise the account is emptied at once
128077.e: With an IBAN people can pay money into an account, but cannot take any out. Your PIN and passwords, on the other hand, stay secret.
128077.m: Share your IBAN, yes; your PIN, never.

128078.q: What comes in a Swiss IBAN after “CH” and the two check digits?
a: A number for the bank, then the account number
128078.e: After the country code and the check digits comes the bank's number. Then comes the actual account number.

128079.q: What are the two check digits in an IBAN for?
a: They help to spot typing mistakes
They show the age of the account
128079.e: If an IBAN is typed wrongly, the check digits no longer match. The online banking then shows an error.

128080.q: Which letters does the IBAN of an account in Liechtenstein start with?
128080.e: Every country has its own code. For Liechtenstein it is LI, for Switzerland CH.

128081.q: What do you need at least to transfer money to someone?
128081.e: For a transfer you give the IBAN, the name and the amount. You never need the other person's passwords or PIN.
128081.m: IBAN, name, amount: off it goes.

128082.q: What is the difference between a deposit and a transfer?
a: A deposit uses cash, a transfer goes from account to account
There is no difference between them
A transfer only works with coins
128082.e: For a deposit you take cash to the bank or post office. A transfer sends money without cash from one account to another.

128083.q: What is a credit to your account?
a: Money going out of the account
128083.e: A credit increases your balance, for example when your wages arrive. The opposite is a debit.

128084.q: Which payment is a standing order best suited to?
128084.e: A standing order regularly pays the same amount to the same person. That suits rent or pocket money well.

128085.q: Where can you pay cash into an account in Switzerland?
a: At the bank counter or a deposit machine
128085.e: You can pay in cash at the counter or at special machines. You can also do it at post office counters.
128085.m: Cash in, at the counter or a machine.

128086.q: Why should you check everything again before confirming a transfer?
a: Getting money back from a wrong transfer is difficult
Because otherwise the bank charges a fine
Because otherwise the transfer is made twice
Because otherwise you get more interest
128086.e: Once the money is in the wrong account, you have to go to a lot of trouble to claim it back. A careful look at the IBAN and amount saves hassle.

128087.q: What is shown in the middle of the QR code on a Swiss QR-bill?
128087.e: The Swiss cross shows that it is a QR code for Swiss bills. That way you recognise it at once.

128088.q: What is a particularly easy way to pay a QR-bill?
a: Scan the QR code with your banking app
Type in all the details by hand
Put the bill into a cash machine
Send the amount in cash in a letter
128088.e: The banking app reads the IBAN, amount and reference from the QR code. You only have to check and confirm.

128089.q: Which details are contained in the QR code of a QR-bill?
a: The IBAN, the recipient and the amount, among others
128089.e: The code contains all the payment details. That way no typing mistakes happen when entering them.
128089.m: The whole payment is in the code.
